findings.title: [P2] Restore one-time ID lookup; current code is O(n·m) with n temporary arrays
findings.body: `current.map(candidate => candidate.id)` now runs inside the `.filter()` callback — once per element of `previous`. For `n = previous.length` and `m = current.length`, runtime regresses from O(n + m) (single `Set` build plus hash lookups) to O(n·m) linear scans, and each iteration allocates a fresh `m`-element array (Θ(n·m) total allocation versus one `m`-element array before). Worst case hits when IDs don't match, which is exactly the common reconcile case where items were removed. For a collection-diffing helper that may see large inputs, this causes substantial CPU and GC pressure. Restore the hoisted structure, e.g. build `const currentIds = new Set(current.map(c => c.id))` once before filtering. Behavior for plain arrays is unchanged, so this is a pure performance fix.

findings.title: [P3] New code requires ES2016 (`Array.prototype.includes`) where the old code needed only ES2015
findings.body: The removed implementation used only ES2015 features (`Set`, `map`, `filter`); `includes` is ES2016. Consumers compiling with `lib: ["es2015"]` would now get TS2550, and ES2015-era runtimes would throw at runtime. This repo has no `tsconfig`/`package.json`, so no in-repo configuration is affected — relevant only if this file is consumed with a pinned ES2015 target. Worth confirming the intended language level, or sidestepped entirely by restoring the `Set`-based check.

findings.title: [P3] Snapshot current IDs before filtering; ids are now re-read n times
findings.body: The old code evaluated each `current` item's `id` exactly once (when building the `Set`); the new code re-reads every current ID once per `previous` element. For plain data properties this is unobservable, but if `Item.id` is a getter, proxy trap, or mutated mid-call, the repeated reads make the result inconsistent — e.g. a getter returning different values across reads can flip membership decisions between iterations where the snapshot version was stable. Requires exotic inputs (`Item` is only referenced, not defined, in this fixture), hence P3; hoisting the ID collection outside the filter restores the snapshot semantics along with the linear runtime.
